entities.summary:
Gereon of Cologne, who may have been a soldier, was martyred at Cologne by beheading, probably in the early 4th century.

Born in Roman Germany around 280 CE, Gereon became a prominent figure in the Christian underground during the Roman Empire's persecution of Christians.

Gereon's leadership of the Cologne Christian community and his alleged involvement in a plot to assassinate Roman officials made him a target for Roman authorities, who eventually put him to death in 304 CE.

Gereon's martyrdom at Cologne had a lasting impact on the city's Christian heritage and marked the beginning of a centuries-long tradition of devotion to the saint.
